captive_summary: Puerto Bahía (Ecopetrol / Sociedad Portuaria Puerto Bahía, Cartagena) is a proposed FSRU import terminal targeting a December 2026 start (300 GBTUD capacity), but as of the most recent reporting (May 2026) the FSRU vessel itself has not yet been contracted or named — "la plataforma aún no cuenta con la unidad flotante de regasificación (FSRU)" (valoraanalitik) and El Espectador independently describes the FSRU "contractual closing" as a still-future milestone. With no vessel identified, there is no published spec (onboard generation or otherwise) to assess.
confirmed_how: valoraanalitik.com (25-May-2026, ANI/ANLA licensing update): “La plataforma aún no cuenta con la unidad flotante de regasificación (FSRU), pero esta podría llegar a finales de 2026 o durante 2027.” El Espectador (25-May-2026), independently, on the FSRU: “uno de los puntos centrales será el cierre contractual del FSRU” (future milestone) and describes the imported gas as feeding “generación térmica, industria y consumo residencial” nationally — general market supply, not a dedicated colocated plant. Neither source, nor Mundo Marítimo's coverage of the same execution announcement, describes any on-site power generation equipment for the terminal itself.

gogpt_prior_assessment: Nearest GOGPT plants are Cartagena power station (203 MW, 3 units, operating, 8.36 km) and Mamonal power station (100 MW, 2 units, operating, 8.95 km) — both pre-existing merchant/industrial plants in Cartagena's Mamonal industrial corridor, well outside fenceline distance and with no documented supply linkage to the not-yet-built FSRU. Not this terminal's captive power. info_url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia (Mamonal industrial zone context; GOGPT-side plant identity itself is out of scope here).

Also serves crude/refined products/LPG per one valoraanalitik piece, i.e. a multi-product port, not LNG-only.
notes: Genuine active proposal (licensed, funded, under execution) — not a screen. Revisit once the FSRU vessel is contracted/named, since a named vessel usually has a citable onboard-generation spec (FSRU-onboard convention).

captive_summary: Under construction at Buenaventura/Buga, Valle del Cauca. The offshore/floating element is an Exmar (Belgian) floating storage and discharge UNIT (FSU) moored in Buenaventura bay — explicitly NOT an FSRU: it receives LNG from carriers and discharges into ISO tanks, with no onboard regasification. The ISO tanks are trucked ~130 km inland to an onshore plant in Buga where regasification (vaporizers) actually occurs. No source found describes the power source (grid vs. on-site generation) for either the FSU or the Buga plant, so the existence of captive gas generation cannot be confirmed or ruled out.
confirmed_how: valoraanalitik.com (19-Sep-2025, ‘Planta regasificadora del Pacífico tiene socio belga’): Exmar signed a five-year charter to deploy a “unidad flotante de almacenamiento y descarga de gas natural licuado” (floating storage and discharge unit) at Buenaventura bay; LNG is discharged into isotanks, barged to the port, trucked to Buga, and “allí el gas volverá a su estado gaseoso” (regasification happens at the Buga plant, not aboard the vessel). Capacity 60 GBTUD. No mention anywhere in this or subsequent 2026 construction-update coverage (Yahoo Noticias, Portafolio, El Tiempo, Caracol Radio — all reporting 80%+ completion as of Jul-2026) of vaporizer power source, on-site generators, or grid connection for the Buga plant.
gogpt_prior_assessment: Andes Energy power station (400 MW, 2 units, gogpt_captive=False, status shelved-inferred ~2y) sits only 0.44 km away — unusually close. No source found in this search establishes a direct pipeline/contractual link between Andes Energy and this LNG terminal; Andes Energy appears to be a separate (currently shelved) merchant thermal project. Given the extreme proximity and shared Buenaventura-area gas theme, this pairing is worth a dedicated look in a future batch to confirm whether Andes Energy was originally conceived as this terminal's offtake (a PowerPlantsSupplied candidate) rather than assuming coincidence. info_url: https://www.gem.wiki/Andes_Energy_power_station (GOGPT record, not a citation for GEM — nav only).
gogpt_candidate_basis: No generating equipment is documented at either the FSU or the Buga plant; nothing citable to add.
status_or_other_findings: GEM's 'vessel' field for this terminal reads 'Tura/El Viche' — could not corroborate either as the Exmar vessel's actual name in any source found (searches for ‘Tura’ + Exmar returned nothing on-topic); flag for a follow-on Update batch to pin down the actual FSU vessel identity/IMO. Multiple mid-2026 sources agree the plant is >80% complete with a target of operations by Nov-2026 (regasification start) / late 2026.
notes: Construction status and 2026 startup timeline are well corroborated across many outlets; the captive-power question specifically is the gap — recommend a targeted follow-up citing an ANLA/CVC environmental permit or the Buga plant's electrical interconnection filing if one becomes available.
